The site is Atlas Roasters — Single-Origin Coffee Subscription Manager, a web-shop web application for Single-origin coffee subscription renewal and grind preference.

Owner brief: "Our independent coffee roastery has an online subscription renewal page where subscribers update their roast selections and grind preferences, but customers report that updates vanish on refresh. Repair the app so customer selections are saved to the server, form errors are announced properly to assistive technologies, and pressing enter does not trigger an accidental early submit."

Locale & copy conventions (en-GB): Use £ prices, British English spelling, day-month dates and .co.uk-style invented domains. Today's date is 11 October 2026; date all entries, bookings, deadlines, and activity in the weeks after 11 October 2026.

Visual identity & layout lock: Match the exact brand header, logo treatment, navigation bar, typography, card geometry, and light colour palette of the attached reference image (docs/design/training/tr-26/reference.jpg).

Art direction: Atlas Roasters — Single-Origin Coffee Subscription Manager: the page for single-origin coffee subscription renewal and grind preference, in a light palette, recognisable by its own token prefix rather than by a shared template.

Use this exact Light Mode colour palette: #261814 (ar-roast), #b45309 (ar-gold), #ffffff (ar-card), #e7e5e4 (ar-border), #fafaf9 (ar-bg), #292524 (ar-text), #78716c (ar-muted). The primary accent colour carries the single primary action.

Structural constants: control-radius 8px, content-frame 1100px, control-border 1px solid var(--ar-border), page-padding 1.5rem. Keep every form control clearly identifiable in its unfocused state with a distinct background fill or icon cue.

Strictly avoid: a price or total that cannot be traced back to a listed item; a second accent colour competing with the primary action; placeholder text standing in for a visible label; a modal or step wizard hiding part of the form; colour alone carrying an error with no message naming the field.

STEP 1 OF 4 (LIGHT MODE) — INITIAL OVERVIEW & READY WORKSPACE:

Render the initial landing state of Atlas Roasters — Single-Origin Coffee Subscription Manager as a visitor first meets it on the primary workspace. Top-to-bottom structure: a brand header, then a navigation bar, then a main content area, then a content section, then the working form, then a footer.

Show the active overview/dashboard/ledger/catalogue surface populated with realistic, internally consistent records and totals, alongside the ready-to-use interactive form with visible labels for every control ("Subscriber name", "Bean selection", "Grind preference", "Delivery frequency", "Bags per delivery", "Delivery notes").

User journey context: Open existing coffee subscription profile and review currently selected beans and grind level. Modify grind preference to espresso and update bag delivery frequency. Save updated subscription preferences and reload the page to verify settings remain stored.

Include editorial photography where appropriate to the subject, a concise social-proof or status summary row, and the complete site footer.
